incidents.vector: Iranian-affiliated actors manipulated internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (PLCs) at US water, energy and government targets, per a six-agency joint advisory (FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA, DOE, Cyber Command).
incidents.impact: Victim organizations confirmed operational disruptions and financial losses; activity has continued since at least March despite a US–Iran ceasefire, with IRGC-linked groups vowing to resume attacks.

incidents.vector: Zero-day authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-50751, CVSS 9.3) in Check Point Remote Access/Mobile Access VPN using the deprecated IKEv1 protocol let attackers establish VPN sessions without valid credentials.
incidents.impact: A few dozen organizations were targeted; Check Point tied at least one post-exploitation case to a Qilin ransomware affiliate. Exploited in the wild since May 7, with activity surging in early June.

incidents.vector: NSO deployed spearphishing and social-engineering links to drive targets to external sites and created test accounts on WhatsApp, in violation of an October court injunction barring it from attacking the platform.
incidents.impact: Meta detected and disrupted the campaign after user reports and filed a contempt-of-court complaint; the activity resembled prior 1-click Pegasus phishing infections.

incidents.vector: An eight-month Kremlin-linked influence campaign (Matryoshka, part of the Doppelganger operation) spread fabricated news, manipulated videos and bot activity, plus hoax bomb threats to polling stations.
incidents.impact: Researchers called it one of the largest Russia-linked disinformation efforts in years; despite it, the pro-European Civil Contract party won ~50% of the vote, defeating the pro-Russian party.

incidents.victim: US law, professional and financial services firms
incidents.vector: Silent Ransom Group (UNC3753 / Luna Moth) used voice phishing, IT-helpdesk impersonation and remote-access tools — and in some cases in-person office visits with USB drives — to reach and exfiltrate sensitive data.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations hit between January and May; the group moved from initial contact to data theft and extortion in under an hour in recent cases, demanding ransom under threat of public leaks.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of PAN-OS authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 in GlobalProtect portal/gateway components let unauthenticated attackers establish VPN connections; added to CISA's KEV catalog May 29.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and a small number of successful gateway-connected sessions; no post-access lateral movement confirmed yet. A public PoC release has driven follow-on scanning.

incidents.vector: Phishing, malvertising and SEO campaigns impersonated AI brands (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, DeepSeek) with account- and billing-themed lures, using redirect chains and adversary-in-the-middle pages to steal credentials, tokens and card data.
incidents.impact: One ChatGPT-themed wave sent up to 100,000 emails in a day; a Claude-themed AiTM campaign hit users at 2,000+ organizations (62% US). Initial-access broker Storm-3075 used AI-themed malvertising to deliver signed malware.

incidents.victim: GitHub and public GitHub developer ecosystem
incidents.vector: A poisoned Nx Console VS Code extension (CVE-2026-48027) auto-updated onto developer machines, compromising a GitHub employee's device; the separate 'Megalodon' campaign injected malicious GitHub Action workflows to harvest CI/CD secrets.
incidents.impact: Internal GitHub repositories were accessed and exfiltrated, and CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials and tokens were harvested across public repos; CISA urged secret rotation and forensic review of pipelines.

incidents.vector: Official Red Hat NPM accounts were compromised and used to push a self-spreading malicious worm through dozens of packages.
incidents.impact: The worm spreads machine-to-machine, stealing sensitive credentials to enable further data theft across developer environments.

incidents.vector: Charter's name was listed on the ShinyHunters dark-web leak portal; the telco subsequently confirmed a security breach.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a breach after being named by the extortion group; the scope of stolen data has not yet been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Attackers used credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real-estate data as the entry point into the state registry.
incidents.impact: About 600,000 records were stolen, including real names, cadastral information and other real-estate details.

incidents.vector: Operation FlutterBridge ran a large Google Ads malvertising campaign via shell companies, distributing the Flutter-based FlutterShell backdoor disguised as podcast and PDF apps (signed and Apple-notarized).
incidents.impact: FlutterShell delivers adware plus backdoor capabilities (shell execution, file access, environment exfiltration); some variants weaponize AI summarization features to route documents through attacker servers. Google suspended the advertiser accounts.

incidents.victim: Instagram (Obama White House, US Space Force accounts)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI support assistant into adding an attacker email to target accounts during the password-reset flow, using a VPN IP near the victim's hometown to bypass checks.
incidents.impact: High-value Instagram accounts including the Obama White House and the US Space Force's senior enlisted leader were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian messages; accounts with MFA enabled defeated the exploit, which Meta has since patched.

incidents.vector: The Play ransomware group claims to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network and is extorting the company.
incidents.impact: Play is publicly extorting MyPillow over allegedly stolen financial documents; the company has not yet confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: A publicly exposed cloud server with no password left inmate-related scanned documents accessible online for at least a week.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images — including driver's licenses and legal and financial documents — were exposed before the server was secured.

incidents.victim: Australian MP Zali Steggall and staff
incidents.vector: A suspected foreign state actor breached the WhatsApp account of an independent Australian MP and three staffers, believed to be part of a Russian campaign targeting politicians' Signal and WhatsApp accounts.
incidents.impact: The MP's and staffers' messaging accounts were compromised in March; attribution to Russia is suspected but unconfirmed.
